title: New skip/decision branches in tasks workflows need a workflow.patched marker; skip queue read for terminal PRs
answers: How do I add a new skip condition to the process_task workflow without breaking replay?
Why is workflow.patched used alongside a new activity output field?
Why does get_pr_babysit_snapshot skip the merge queue read for closed PRs?
body:
When a new activity-output field changes a workflow decision, gate the branch with `workflow.patched(<id>)` as well as the flag. During rolling deploys a new activity worker can record the flag while an old workflow worker still dispatches, so replay must keep the old path. See `_PATCH_ID_MERGE_QUEUE_SKIP` in process_task/workflow.py and in task_management/workflow.py (each file has its own constant, separate workflow classes).
Test both paths by monkeypatching `process_task_workflow_module.workflow.patched` (see `test_merge_queue_skip_follows_the_patch_marker` in process_task/tests/test_ci_follow_up_decision.py).
Optional new fields on activity outputs default to False (`GetPrContextOutput`, `PRSnapshot.from_raw` uses `is True`). Activity output dataclasses state `frozen=` (devex semgrep).
Extra GitHub reads must skip closed/merged PRs (`get_pr_babysit_snapshot.py`, `get_pr_context`), so a flaky read cannot fail the terminal tick.
